subject: Post-signature MAP: implementation cadence, canary, migration & training (Falkon AI)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarika Patel <sarika.patel@falkon.ai>, Tom Adler <tom.adler@falkon.ai>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP kickoff — post-signature implementation & canary plan

Sarika / Tom — congrats again on signing. Attaching an initial MAP draft (MAP_Falkon_v1.xlsx) & a proposed training agenda. This thread will track the post-signature plan embedded in the MAP: rollout windows, canary execution, migration steps, and enablement.

High-level timeline (proposal):
- Week 0 (Mar 8–12): Contract handoff & environment provisioning
- Week 1 (Mar 15–19): Canary window (sandbox -> small live traffic)
- Week 3 (Mar 29–Apr 2): Migration pilot + validation checks
- Week 5 (Apr 12–16): Full cutover & knowledge transfer training

Immediate asks: 1) Confirm your preferred migration weekend (Mar 26–28 or Apr 9–11). 2) Confirm training attendees and whether you want remote or on-site format. 3) Any required procurement kickoff or SOC evidence needed before provisioning?

Attachments: MAP_Falkon_v1.xlsx (MAP draft), training_agenda.pdf

Thanks — I’ll sync internal owners once you confirm dates.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
From: Sarika Patel <sarika.patel@falkon.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Adler <tom.adler@falkon.ai>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 05 Mar 2027 10:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — post-signature implementation & canary plan

Hi Vanessa — thanks, excited to get started. A few quick notes:
- We prefer the migration weekend Apr 9–11 (gives us two weeks to prep).
- Training should be remote initially; we may request an optional on-site workshop later. Expected attendees: Sarika, Tom, 2 infra engineers, 1 security lead (procurement looped separately).
- On SOC / procurement: procurement@falkon.ai will need the SOC2 report and a runbook for data handling. I’ve CC'd them on this thread.

Also — for the canary, what minimum traffic do you need to validate performance SLA (p50/p95)? We’ll aim to allocate a small slice of production traffic but want to understand the gating criteria.

Thanks,
Sarika
Head of Platform, Falkon AI
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Sarika Patel <sarika.patel@falkon.ai>
Cc: Tom Adler <tom.adler@falkon.ai>, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 08 Mar 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — post-signature implementation & canary plan

Sarika — great, Apr 9–11 for migration works from our side. Quick answers:
- Canary gating: we usually run a 48–72h canary with 5–10% production traffic to validate latency (p50 < 120ms, p95 < 350ms under typical load) and error rate (<0.5%). If those metrics hold and quality checks from Grace’s eval pass, we expand traffic incrementally.
- SOC2 / runbook: attaching a short evidence index and our standard SOC2 executive summary for procurement to reference.

Next internal assignments (for transparency):
- Grace: lead evaluation & quality checkpoints (eval-checklist.md)
- Rishi: runtime & canary configuration + rollback policy (canary-config.yaml)
- Priyom: cutover orchestration and handoff cadence; will coordinate support coverage windows.

I’ll update the MAP draft with these targets and circulate a refined plan by EOD Wednesday.

— Vanessa
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sarika Patel <sarika.patel@falkon.ai>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — post-signature implementation & canary plan

Thanks Vanessa / Sarika — I’ve attached the evaluation checklist and a short rack of prompt/eval pairs we’ll use during the canary. Key gating items I’ll validate during the 48–72h window:
- Functional correctness: automated evals on a representative test set (pass rate >= 95%)
- Latency & errors: confirm p50/p95 and error window targets (see Vanessa)
- Quality regressions: human spot-checks (3 engineers, 20 prompts each)
- Data retention & masking verification: ensure requests with PII patterns are redacted per runbook

If the gate fails, rollback to the prior model variant and we’ll convene a 1-hour postmortem. I’ll also post a short scorecard to the MAP spreadsheet after each day.

Attachment: eval-checklist.md

— Grace
Senior Applied ML, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sarika Patel <sarika.patel@falkon.ai>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff — post-signature implementation & canary plan

Quick notes from the runtime side:
- Canary config attached (canary-config.yaml). I recommend starting at 5% traffic with a conservative batching profile (max_batch=8, max_latency_ms=50) to protect latency during warm-up.
- Rollback policy: automatic fallback to the previous pinned model if p95 latency exceeds threshold for 2 consecutive 15-min windows or error rate > 0.5%.
- Migration considerations: if you’re doing bulk data migration for fine-tuning or embeddings, let us know the transfer mechanism (S3 link vs. direct DB replication). For S3, provide a pre-signed bucket and we’ll run a dry transfer during Week 1.

I’ll merge the canary config into the MAP and circulate MAP_Falkon_final.xlsx by tomorrow morning.

— Rishi
Runtime Engineering, Redwood Inference
